skipped_lines.text: gallantry to the last. From Appomattox the rcr^inicnt returned to Peters-
burg, and after a week's rest marched to the neighborhood of Washington,
where it remained in camp until its final muster out of service, on the IGth of
June. A detachment of this regiment was consolidated with parts of the First
Cavalry, and remained in service until the 7tli of August, when it was mus-
tered out at Louisville, Ky. In his farewell order to the Seventeenth, General
Devin says : "In five successive campaigns, and in over three score engage-
from your State none has a brighter record, none has more freely shed its blood
on every battle field from Gettysburg to Appomattox. Your gallant deeds
will be ever fresh in the memory of your comrades of the Iron Brigade and
the First Division. Soldiers, Farewell !"
